front_blocks.md: How are sound waves produced?

back_blocks.md: Sound waves are produced by **vibrating** (or oscillating) sources.

cards.front_md: How are sound waves produced?
cards.back_md: Sound waves are produced by **vibrating** (or oscillating) sources.

front_blocks.md: What is the name of the region of a sound wave where the pressure is lower due to particles being spaced further apart? **(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: The region of a sound wave with **lower pressure**, due to particles being spaced further apart, is called a **rarefaction**.

cards.front_md: What is the name of the region of a sound wave where the pressure is lower due to particles being spaced further apart? **(Extended Tier Only)**
cards.back_md: The region of a sound wave with **lower pressure**, due to particles being spaced further apart, is called a **rarefaction**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Sound waves are transverse waves. **(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Sound waves are **longitudinal** waves, travelling as a series of **compressions** and **rarefactions**.

front_blocks.md: What is the name of the region of a sound wave where the pressure is higher due to particles being closer together? **(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: The region of a sound wave with **higher pressure**, due to particles being closer together, is called a **compression**.

cards.front_md: What is the name of the region of a sound wave where the pressure is higher due to particles being closer together? **(Extended Tier Only)**

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Sound is a type of pressure wave. **(Extended Tier Only)**

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Sound waves consist of **compressions** (regions of higher pressure) and **rarefactions** (regions of lower pressure), so the pressure of the air varies with the wave.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Sound waves can travel through a vacuum.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Sound waves need a **medium** to travel through, so they cannot travel through a **vacuum** where there are no particles.

front_blocks.md: What happens when a sound wave comes into contact with a solid?

back_blocks.md: The wave vibrations are **transferred** to the solid, making it vibrate. For example, sound waves can cause a drinking glass to vibrate, and too much vibration can cause the glass to shatter.

front_blocks.md: What is the typical speed of sound in air?

back_blocks.md: The speed of sound in air is about **340 m/s**.

back_blocks.md: Sound travels fastest in **solids**, at around 5000 m/s.

front_blocks.md: Which equation is used to calculate the speed of sound from distance and time measurements?

back_blocks.md: $\text{average speed} = \frac{\text{distance moved}}{\text{time taken}}$

front_blocks.md: What is the relationship between the **frequency** of a sound wave and its **pitch**?

back_blocks.md: Sounds with a **high frequency** (or short wavelength) have a **high pitch**, and sounds with a **low frequency** (or long wavelength) have a **low pitch**.

front_blocks.md: Define the term **ultrasound**.
